title: School and College Enrollment Validation
text:
This site validates the PopulationSim synthetic population — the household/person microdata underlying WFRC’s travel demand model — against real K-12 and college enrollment, for the Wasatch Front region (Box Elder, Davis, Weber, Salt Lake, and Utah counties). School enrollment is compared at the school district level; college enrollment at the county level.
PopulationSim doesn’t control on school enrollment directly, so each comparison is made two ways: against the synthetic population’s uncontrolled enrollment-status label (the real test of how well the synthetic population reflects actual enrollment), and against its controlled age-band population (a sanity bound — age-eligible should meet or exceed enrolled, not match it exactly).

Geography — builds the block-level crosswalk (county, district, TAZ, and matched school/college IDs) that every later step joins against. MAZ is a placeholder for now — WFRC hasn’t published it yet.
Enrollment — real K-12 and college enrollment, from state and federal sources.
Synthetic Population — PopulationSim’s synthetic enrollment estimates, rolled up to the same district/county geography.
Validation — the comparison itself.

title: Synthetic Population
text:
This script produces the “synthetic” half of the validation schema — PopulationSim’s estimate of how many K-12 students and college students live in each district/county, to compare against the real enrollment numbers from 2_enrollment.qmd.

Objective: for each district, count synthetic persons two ways — by enrollment status (PersonType_Label == "K-12 student", uncontrolled in PopulationSim, so this is the real test) and by age band (5-17, a controlled variable, so a sanity bound rather than an exact match). Same two-way count for colleges by county, using "University student" and a college-age band, combining PopulationSim’s regular household persons with its separate dorm/group-quarters student file.
What it reads: PopulationSim’s synthetic person/household output (local-only — gitignored in the TDM-INP-PopulationSim repo, so this script needs a local path to wherever that output actually lives on this machine, not a repo-relative path) and the block-level crosswalk from 1_geography.qmd.
MAZ/TAZ join: PopulationSim’s output is keyed at MAZ/TAZ level, not Census block. The crosswalk from 1_geography.qmd now carries TAZID per block (sourced from WFRC’s WasatchFrontTAZ feature service), so district/county rollup can go through TAZID rather than needing a direct MAZ-to-block join — still need to confirm PopulationSim’s output is keyed at this same TAZID (not a different internal MAZ id) before relying on it.
Box Elder: handled last — the MPO/TDM model region only partially covers the county, so its synthetic counts need to be clipped to the model boundary (1_geography.qmd’s model_boundary layer) rather than compared at full-county scope like the other four counties.
Output: synthetic enrollment-status and age-band counts, by district and by county, written to _outputs/.

title: Geography
Geography
text:
Overview
This script builds the geographic crosswalk that every later step in this project joins against.

Objective: tie every Census block in the Wasatch Front region (Box Elder, Davis, Weber, Salt Lake, and Utah counties) to the school district and county it falls in, and to the K-12 school(s) and college(s) located in it — so that PopulationSim’s synthetic population (3_synthetic.qmd) and real enrollment data (2_enrollment.qmd) can both be rolled up to district/county level as exact joins, with no area-weighting or estimation involved.
What it pulls: county, school district, Travel Analysis Zone (TAZ), and Census block boundaries; K-12 school and college locations from both UGRC/SGID (the state-preferred source) and NCES (kept alongside, not as a replacement, so schools and colleges can also be joined back to federal CCD/IPEDS data by ID); and the WFRC/MAG travel demand model boundary, used later to handle Box Elder County’s partial coverage in that model. TAZ boundaries come from WFRC’s WasatchFrontTAZ feature service rather than the TDM-GEO-AnalysisZones repo directly, so the pull stays current without tracking that repo’s releases — TAZID is what resolves 3_synthetic.qmd’s open question of how to join PopulationSim’s MAZ/TAZ-keyed output to this block-level crosswalk.
Output: a single block-level crosswalk (_data/intermediate/crosswalk.csv) carrying each block’s county, district, TAZ, and matched school/college IDs from every source. Section 10 checks how well each field matched (the coverage table in Section 10) and maps the study area (Figure 1).

text:
1. County boundaries


Show code
county_boundary_path = paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "county_boundary.gpkg"

# 1. Download only if not already cached locally
if not county_boundary_path.exists():
    all_counties = counties(state=state_fips, year=2023, cache=True).to_crs(constants["crs"])
    all_counties.to_file(county_boundary_path)

# 2. Always read from local storage -- full state, not just our 5 counties. Every later section
#    tags its schools/colleges/districts against all_counties so those statewide .gpkg caches carry
#    a correct county_fips everywhere, not just inside our study area; bound_counties (below) is the
#    5-county-filtered version used to restrict the crosswalk itself.
all_counties = gpd.read_file(county_boundary_path)

county_list_sql = ", ".join(f"'{fips}'" for fips in county_fips)

bound_counties = gpd.read_file(
    county_boundary_path, sql=f"SELECT * FROM county_boundary WHERE COUNTYFP IN ({county_list_sql})"
)




Show code
bound_counties.explore()

title: Geography
text:
2. School district boundaries


Show code
district_boundary_path = paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "school_district_boundary.gpkg"

# 1. Download only if not already cached locally
if not district_boundary_path.exists():
    all_districts = gpd.read_postgis(
        "select * from boundaries.school_district_boundaries", opensgid_engine, geom_col="shape"
    ).to_crs(constants["crs"])

    all_districts["county_fips"] = gpd.sjoin(
        all_districts.set_geometry(all_districts.centroid),
        all_counties[["COUNTYFP", "geometry"]],
        predicate="within",
        how="left",
    )["COUNTYFP"]

    all_districts.to_file(district_boundary_path)

# 2. Read + filter in one step, pushed down to SQLite
county_list_sql = ", ".join(f"'{fips}'" for fips in county_fips)

bound_districts = gpd.read_file(
    district_boundary_path,
    sql=f"SELECT * FROM school_district_boundary WHERE county_fips IN ({county_list_sql})",
)




Show code

title: Geography
text:
3. Travel Analysis Zone (TAZ) boundaries


Show code
taz_boundary_path = paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "taz_boundary.gpkg"

# 1. Download only if not already cached locally
if not taz_boundary_path.exists():
    taz_url = (
        "https://services1.arcgis.com/taguadKoI1XFwivx/ArcGIS/rest/services/"
        "WasatchFrontTAZ/FeatureServer/0/query"
    )
    taz_pages = []
    offset = 0
    while True:
        page = gpd.read_file(
            f"{taz_url}?where=1=1&outFields=*&f=geojson"
            f"&orderByFields=FID&resultOffset={offset}&resultRecordCount=2000"
        )
        if page.empty:
            break
        taz_pages.append(page)
        offset += len(page)
        if len(page) < 2000:
            break
    all_taz = pd.concat(taz_pages, ignore_index=True).to_crs(constants["crs"])

    count_resp = requests.get(f"{taz_url}?where=1=1&returnCountOnly=true&f=json").json()
    assert len(all_taz) == count_resp["count"], (len(all_taz), count_resp["count"])

    all_taz["county_fips"] = all_taz["CO_FIPS"].astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(3)

    all_taz.to_file(taz_boundary_path)

# 2. Read + filter in one step, pushed down to SQLite
county_list_sql = ", ".join(f"'{fips}'" for fips in county_fips)

bound_taz = gpd.read_file(
    taz_boundary_path, sql=f"SELECT * FROM taz_boundary WHERE county_fips IN ({county_list_sql})"
)




Show code
bound_taz.explore()

title: Geography
text:
5. Census blocks


Show code
block_boundary_path = paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "block_boundary.gpkg"
block_counties_path = paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "block_boundary.counties.txt"

# Auto-invalidate the cache if constants["counties"] has changed since it was built -- pygris'
# blocks() call below is scoped to the CURRENT county list at fetch time (unlike every other
# cached layer in this file, which fetches statewide and filters at read-time), so a stale cache
# here would silently miss any newly-added county's blocks instead of erroring.
current_counties = sorted(county_fips)
cached_counties = (
    block_counties_path.read_text().splitlines() if block_counties_path.exists() else []
)
if block_boundary_path.exists() and current_counties != cached_counties:
    block_boundary_path.unlink()

# 1. Download only if not already cached locally
if not block_boundary_path.exists():
    all_blocks = blocks(state=state_fips, county=county_fips, year=2023, cache=True).to_crs(
        constants["crs"]
    )

    all_blocks["district_name"] = gpd.sjoin(
        all_blocks.set_geometry(all_blocks.centroid),
        bound_districts[["name", "geometry"]],
        predicate="within",
        how="left",
    )["name"]

    all_blocks["TAZID"] = gpd.sjoin(
        all_blocks.set_geometry(all_blocks.centroid),
        bound_taz[["TAZID", "geometry"]],
        predicate="within",
        how="left",
    )["TAZID"]

    all_blocks["maz_id"] = gpd.sjoin(
        all_blocks.set_geometry(all_blocks.centroid),
        bound_maz[["maz_id", "geometry"]],
        predicate="within",
        how="left",
    )["maz_id"]

    all_blocks.to_file(block_boundary_path)
    block_counties_path.write_text("\n".join(current_counties))

# 2. Read + filter in one step, pushed down to SQLite
county_list_sql = ", ".join(f"'{fips}'" for fips in county_fips)

bound_blocks = gpd.read_file(
    block_boundary_path, sql=f"SELECT * FROM block_boundary  WHERE COUNTYFP20 IN({county_list_sql})"
)




Show code
bound_blocks.explore()

    predicate="within",
    how="left",
)[["xid", "GEOID20"]].rename(columns={"xid": "College ID"})

nces_public_block_match = gpd.sjoin(
    nces_public_schools[["NCESSCH", "geometry"]],
    bound_blocks[["GEOID20", "geometry"]],
    predicate="within",
    how="left",
)[["NCESSCH", "GEOID20"]].rename(columns={"NCESSCH": "NCES School ID"})

nces_private_block_match = gpd.sjoin(
    nces_private_schools[["PPIN", "geometry"]],
    bound_blocks[["GEOID20", "geometry"]],
    predicate="within",
    how="left",
)[["PPIN", "GEOID20"]].rename(columns={"PPIN": "NCES Private School ID"})

nces_college_block_match = gpd.sjoin(
    nces_colleges[["UNITID", "geometry"]],
    bound_blocks[["GEOID20", "geometry"]],
    predicate="within",
    how="left",
)[["UNITID", "GEOID20"]].rename(columns={"UNITID": "NCES College ID"})

crosswalk = (
    bound_blocks[["GEOID20", "COUNTYFP20", "district_name", "TAZID", "maz_id"]]
    .merge(school_block_match.rename(columns={"schoolid": "School ID"}), on="GEOID20", how="left")
    .merge(college_block_match, on="GEOID20", how="left")
    .merge(nces_public_block_match, on="GEOID20", how="left")
    .merge(nces_private_block_match, on="GEOID20", how="left")
    .merge(nces_college_block_match, on="GEOID20", how="left")
    .rename(
        columns={"GEOID20": "GEOID", "COUNTYFP20": "COUNTYFP", "district_name": "District Name"}
    )
)

crosswalk["School ID"] = crosswalk["School ID"].astype("Int64")
crosswalk["College ID"] = crosswalk["College ID"].astype("Int64")
crosswalk["TAZID"] = crosswalk["TAZID"].astype("Int64")
crosswalk["maz_id"] = crosswalk["maz_id"].astype("Int64")

crosswalk.to_csv(paths["intermediate"] / "crosswalk.csv", index=False)

# either way), but matters in an interactive session where re-running Setup without restarting
# the kernel would otherwise orphan the previous engine's pooled connection to Open SGID.
opensgid_engine.dispose()

title: Enrollment
Enrollment
text:
Overview
This script produces the “real enrollment” half of the validation schema — the numbers PopulationSim’s synthetic population (3_synthetic.qmd) gets compared against.

Objective: get district-level K-12 enrollment and county-level college enrollment from real, non-synthetic sources, joined through the block-level crosswalk built in 1_geography.qmd.
What it pulls: Utah DOE enrollment (public schools only, from UGRC’s own per-school counts), NCES enrollment by district (public via CCD, private via the Private School Universe Survey); USHE (student home ZIP code, not institution location — a different geography than everything else in this project) and NCES/IPEDS enrollment by county.
Known gaps: NCES private-school enrollment is school-location-based, not residence-based, and a handful of statewide online-only private programs still need manual review before being trusted at face value (see section 3); USHE data is Academic Year 2025, not 2023-24 — no 2023-24 USHE extract exists in what WFRC has on file, so this is a real year mismatch against the ~2023 vintage used everywhere else, not an oversight.
Output: one table of district-level enrollment, one table of county-level enrollment, both written to _outputs/.

import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd

import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

paths = {
    "raw": Path("_data/raw/"),
    "intermediate": Path("_data/intermediate/"),
    "output": Path("_outputs/"),
}

constants = {
    "data_year": 2023  # NCES/IPEDS/PSS vintage -- bump this one number in ~4 years
}
year_code = f"{str(constants['data_year'])[-2:]}{str(constants['data_year'] + 1)[-2:]}"

crosswalk = pd.read_csv(paths["intermediate"] / "crosswalk.csv", dtype={"COUNTYFP": str})

section: 1. K-12 — Utah DOE enrollment by district

1. K-12 — Utah DOE enrollment by district


Show code
# Public schools only
ugrc_public_schools = gpd.read_file(
    paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "ugrc_school.gpkg",
    sql="""
        SELECT * FROM ugrc_school
        WHERE privateschool = 'False'
          AND onlineschool IS NOT 'Y'
    """,
)

# Join school -> district via the crosswalk (block-based, spatial) rather than matching the
# school's own `leaname` text against the district boundary's `name` text. Dedup on School ID first:
# the block-level crosswalk repeats 144 schools 2-5 times, which would double-count their enrollment.
crosswalk_schools = crosswalk.dropna(subset=["School ID"]).drop_duplicates(subset=["School ID"])

# Left join, so schools with no crosswalk match are kept visible instead of silently dropped
doe_schools = ugrc_public_schools[["schoolid", "totalk12"]].merge(
    crosswalk_schools[["School ID", "District Name"]],
    how="left",
    left_on="schoolid",
    right_on="School ID",
)

unmatched_doe_schools = doe_schools[doe_schools["District Name"].isna()]
print(
    f"DOE schools with no district match: {len(unmatched_doe_schools)} "
    f"({unmatched_doe_schools['totalk12'].sum():,.0f} students, excluded from district totals)"
)

# groupby drops the unmatched rows (NaN district), so they are excluded from the totals below
doe_enrollment_by_district = (
    doe_schools.groupby("District Name")["totalk12"]
    .sum()
    .rename("doe_enrollment")
    .reset_index()
)

text:
4. Colleges — USHE enrollment by county


Show code
# NOTE: the only USHE data WFRC has on file is Academic Year 2025 (Term 2 / Spring) and Academic Year 2020 (Term 2)
# USHE covers Utah's PUBLIC institutions only. Private institutions (e.g., BYU, Westminster, Ensign)
# are not in USHE and only appear in the IPEDS county totals, so county comparisons are not like-for-like.
# Both full-time and part-time students are kept, matching the WF-TDM college repo (6-CollegeControlTotals.qmd).
ushe = pd.read_excel(paths["raw"] / "ushe" / "WFRC Data Request_Final.xlsx")

ushe_2025_fall = ushe.query("`Academic Year` == 2025 and Term == 2")




Show code
# Scoped to WFRC region institutions/sites only (constants["counties"] in 1_geography.qmd) --
# USHE has no surrogate ID, so (Institution, Site) is the natural key; UGRC's unique ID is `xid`.
# A few sites have no UGRC point of their own and are reassigned to a same-county campus instead --
# "USU - Ogden Center" goes to Weber State's Main Campus xid, NOT USU's own (Cache County) Main
# Campus, since the reassignment target has to match the real site's county, not its institution.
ushe_to_ugrc_xid = {
    ("Salt Lake Community College", "Correctional Facility--West Valley City"): 52,
    ("Salt Lake Community College", "Main Campus"): 4,
    ("Salt Lake Community College", "SLCC - Airport Center"): 4,
    ("Salt Lake Community College", "SLCC - Jordan Campus"): 51,
    ("Salt Lake Community College", "SLCC - Larry H. Miller Campus"): 50,
    ("Salt Lake Community College", "SLCC - South City Center"): 46,
    ("Salt Lake Community College", "SLCC - West Point Center"): 78,
    ("Salt Lake Community College", "SLCC - West Valley City"): 52,
    ("Salt Lake Community College", "SLCC-UU Juniper building at Herriman Campus"): 4,
    ("University Of Utah", "Main Campus"): 7,
    ("University Of Utah", "SLCC-UU Juniper building at Herriman Campus"): 7,
    ("University Of Utah", "UU - Sandy Center"): 7,
    ("Utah State University", "USU - Brigham Center"): 14,
    ("Utah State University", "USU - Ogden Center"): 1,
    ("Utah State University", "USU - Orem Center"): 28,
    ("Utah State University", "USU - Salt Lake Center"): 32,
    ("Utah State University", "USU - Tremonton Center"): 31,
    ("Utah Valley University", "Main Campus"): 5,
    ("Weber State University", "Main Campus"): 1,
    ("Weber State University", "Technical College Campus--Davis"): 56,
    ("Weber State University", "Technical College Campus--Ogden-Weber"): 69,
    ("Weber State University", "University Center--SLCC"): 4,
    ("Weber State University", "WSU - Davis Center"): 37,
    ("Weber State University", "WSU - Farmington Station"): 42,
}

# Everything not in the dict is out-of-region or a non-geographic site (online, other-site, etc.)
ushe_in_region = ushe_2025_fall[
    ushe_2025_fall.set_index(["Institution", "Site"]).index.isin(ushe_to_ugrc_xid)
].assign(xid=lambda df: df.set_index(["Institution", "Site"]).index.map(ushe_to_ugrc_xid))

ugrc_colleges = gpd.read_file(paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "ugrc_college.gpkg")

ushe_enrollment_by_county = (
    ushe_in_region.merge(ugrc_colleges[["xid", "county_fips"]], on="xid")
    .groupby("county_fips")["Headcount"]
    .sum()
    .rename("ushe_enrollment")
    .reset_index()
)

text:
5. Colleges — NCES/IPEDS enrollment by county


Show code
# IPEDS Fall Enrollment distance-education component (EF{year}A_DIST). In-person enrollment is
# students in no distance-ed courses (EFDENON) plus students in some distance-ed / hybrid courses
# (EFDESOM); exclusively online students are excluded because they generate no campus trips.
# Same source and method as the WF-TDM college enrollment repo (5-CollegeEnrollmentIPEDS.qmd).
ipeds_dir = paths["raw"] / "ipeds"
ipeds_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
zip_path = ipeds_dir / f"EF{constants['data_year']}A_DIST.zip"

if not zip_path.exists():
    # The datacenter/data path serves 2023; the tablefiles/zipfiles path used in the WF-TDM repo returns 404
    response = requests.get(
        f"https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/data/EF{constants['data_year']}A_DIST.zip"
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    zip_path.write_bytes(response.content)

# pandas reads the single CSV inside the zip directly, so nothing is extracted to disk
ipeds_dist = pd.read_csv(zip_path)




Show code
# EFDELEV == 1 is the grand-total row for each institution (the other levels are breakdowns)
ipeds_in_person = ipeds_dist.query("EFDELEV == 1").assign(
    in_person=lambda df: df["EFDENON"].fillna(0) + df["EFDESOM"].fillna(0)
)[["UNITID", "in_person"]]

# The seven target colleges from the WF-TDM college repo (6-CollegeControlTotals.qmd), each assigned
# to its county. The other institutions in the crosswalk are left out to match that snapshot.
target_county = {
    230764: "035",  # University of Utah (Salt Lake)
    230746: "035",  # Salt Lake Community College (all five campuses are in Salt Lake County)
    230418: "035",  # Ensign College
    230807: "035",  # Westminster University
    230038: "049",  # Brigham Young University (Utah County)
    230737: "049",  # Utah Valley University (Utah County)
    230782: "057",  # Weber State University (Main campus, Weber County)
}

ipeds_targets = ipeds_in_person[ipeds_in_person["UNITID"].isin(target_county)].assign(
    COUNTYFP=lambda df: df["UNITID"].map(target_county)
)

# Weber State's Davis campus is counted in Davis County, using its share of USHE headcount among
# the two WSU campuses in the repo's split (Main campus and WSU - Davis Center)
wsu_sites = ushe_2025_fall[
    (ushe_2025_fall["Institution"] == "Weber State University")
    & ushe_2025_fall["Site"].isin(["Main Campus", "WSU - Davis Center"])
].groupby("Site")["Headcount"].sum()
wsu_davis_share = wsu_sites["WSU - Davis Center"] / wsu_sites.sum()

wsu_total = ipeds_targets.loc[ipeds_targets["UNITID"] == 230782, "in_person"].item()
wsu_davis_students = round(wsu_total * wsu_davis_share)
ipeds_targets.loc[ipeds_targets["UNITID"] == 230782, "in_person"] = wsu_total - wsu_davis_students
ipeds_targets = pd.concat(
    [
        ipeds_targets,
        pd.DataFrame({"UNITID": [230782], "in_person": [wsu_davis_students], "COUNTYFP": ["011"]}),
    ],
    ignore_index=True,
)

ipeds_enrollment_by_county = (
    ipeds_targets.groupby("COUNTYFP")["in_person"]
    .sum()
    .rename("ipeds_enrollment")
    .reset_index()
)

School Enrollment by School Districts

# Canonical district list -- every district the block-level crosswalk covers, regardless of
# whether a given source has a school in it (left-merging onto this keeps a real data gap visible
# as NaN instead of silently dropping the row via an inner join)
district_list = crosswalk[["District Name"]].dropna().drop_duplicates()

school_enrollment = (
    district_list.merge(doe_enrollment_by_district, on="District Name", how="left")
    .merge(nces_enrollment_by_district, on="District Name", how="left")
    .merge(nces_private_enrollment_by_district, on="District Name", how="left")
)
# No private schools in a district is a real zero, not a gap
school_enrollment["nces_private_enrollment"] = school_enrollment["nces_private_enrollment"].fillna(
    0
)

section: 8. Universities: USHE vs IPEDS by modality
text:
8. Universities: USHE vs IPEDS by modality


Show code
university_names = {
    230764: "University of Utah",
    230746: "Salt Lake Community College",
    230782: "Weber State University",
    230737: "Utah Valley University",
    230038: "Brigham Young University",
    230418: "Ensign College",
    230807: "Westminster University",
}
ushe_names = {
    "University Of Utah": "University of Utah",
    "Salt Lake Community College": "Salt Lake Community College",
    "Weber State University": "Weber State University",
    "Utah Valley University": "Utah Valley University",
}

# IPEDS, fall 2023 (same definitions as section 5)
ipeds_long = (
    ipeds_dist[ipeds_dist["EFDELEV"] == 1]
    .loc[lambda df: df["UNITID"].isin(list(university_names))]
    .assign(
        Institution=lambda df: df["UNITID"].map(university_names),
        **{
            "In-person only": lambda df: df["EFDENON"].fillna(0),
            "Hybrid (some DE)": lambda df: df["EFDESOM"].fillna(0),
            "Online only": lambda df: df["EFDEEXC"].fillna(0),
        },
    )
    .melt(
        id_vars=["Institution"],
        value_vars=["In-person only", "Hybrid (some DE)", "Online only"],
        var_name="Segment",
        value_name="Students",
    )
    .assign(Source="IPEDS")
)

# USHE, Academic Year 2025 Term 2 (full- and part-time). The "taught online" rows are the hybrid
# portion; USHE has no online-only category.
ushe_long = (
    ushe_2025_fall[ushe_2025_fall["Institution"].isin(list(ushe_names))]
    .assign(
        Institution=lambda df: df["Institution"].map(ushe_names),
        Segment=lambda df: df["Site"].eq("This portion of the course is taught online").map(
            {True: "Hybrid (some DE)", False: "In-person only"}
        ),
    )
    .groupby(["Institution", "Segment"], as_index=False)["Headcount"]
    .sum()
    .rename(columns={"Headcount": "Students"})
    .assign(Source="USHE")
)

modality_compare = pd.concat([ipeds_long, ushe_long], ignore_index=True)[
    ["Institution", "Source", "Segment", "Students"]
]
modality_compare.to_csv(paths["intermediate"] / "university_modality_compare.csv", index=False)

title: Validation
text:
This is the page the site is actually built around — where the real enrollment numbers (2_enrollment.qmd) and PopulationSim’s synthetic estimates (3_synthetic.qmd) get compared.

Objective: for each school district, compare real (Utah DOE / NCES) K-12 enrollment against PopulationSim’s synthetic K-12 student count (the real test, since that’s uncontrolled) and against its synthetic age 5-17 population (a sanity bound, since that’s controlled — not expected to match exactly). Same comparison for colleges by county, real (USHE / NCES-IPEDS) vs. synthetic university-student count and college-age population.
What it reads: the two output tables from 2_enrollment.qmd and the two from 3_synthetic.qmd, all from _outputs/.
Box Elder: reported separately from the other four counties, since its real and synthetic numbers are both scoped differently there (model region vs. full county) — a single pooled number would misrepresent it either way.
Output: this page itself — the published comparison tables and charts, not another intermediate file.
